reason: The cited lines show creating a new browser tab and, if a URL parameter is supplied, navigating to that URL, which is a request to an agent/tool-chosen destination and thus supports SINK. They also show including a snapshot / tab header data in the response after navigation, so content controlled by the destination page can be returned, supporting UNTRUSTED. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution. They may return browser/tab/page data, but these lines alone do not establish that the data is non-public host/SaaS/local/intranet content, so SECRET is insufficient.
